blocks.content: 1. Digestive System – Meaning and Need

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Digestion begins in the mouth where salivary amylase breaks down starch into maltose.
The stomach uses hydrochloric acid and pepsin to digest proteins while mucus protects its lining.
The liver secretes bile for emulsification of fats, whereas the pancreas provides trypsin, amylase, and lipase.
Nutrient absorption occurs mostly in the small intestine, assisted by villi and microvilli.
The large intestine absorbs water and minerals, housing bacteria that synthesize vitamins B and K.

blocks.content:
The digestive system is the system of organs responsible for breaking down complex food substances into simpler, absorbable forms.
Food consumed by humans contains carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, and water.
These complex substances cannot be directly used by the body.
Digestion converts them into simple molecules like glucose, amino acids, fatty acids, and glycerol.
These nutrients provide energy, help in growth, repair of tissues, and maintenance of body functions.
The digestive system performs four main functions: ingestion, digestion, absorption, and egestion.
Both mechanical digestion (chewing, churning) and chemical digestion (enzymes) are involved.
2. Human Digestive System – Overview

The human digestive system consists of the alimentary canal and digestive glands.
The alimentary canal is a long muscular tube about 8–10 meters long.
Digestive glands include salivary glands, liver, and pancreas.
Each organ of the digestive system has a specific role.
Proper coordination between organs and enzymes is essential for digestion.
Any disorder in this system affects overall health and nutrition.
3. Alimentary Canal – Parts and Functions

The alimentary canal begins at the mouth and ends at the anus.
Its main parts include mouth, pharynx, esophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine, rectum, and anus.
Food moves through these organs in a definite sequence.
Peristaltic movements help in pushing food forward.
Different regions of the alimentary canal are specialized for digestion or absorption.
Maximum absorption occurs in the small intestine.
4. Mouth and Buccal Cavity

The mouth is the first part of the digestive system.
The buccal cavity contains teeth, tongue, and salivary glands.
Teeth help in mechanical digestion by cutting and grinding food.
Tongue mixes food with saliva and helps in swallowing.
Saliva contains salivary amylase (ptyalin) which converts starch into maltose.
Saliva also contains mucus which lubricates food.
Digestion of carbohydrates begins in the mouth.
5. Pharynx and Esophagus

The pharynx acts as a common passage for food and air.
Food enters the esophagus from the pharynx.
The esophagus is a muscular tube that connects pharynx to stomach.
Food is pushed into the stomach by peristalsis.
Peristalsis is involuntary rhythmic contraction and relaxation of muscles.
No digestion occurs in the esophagus.
Maximum absorption occurs in the small intestine.
6. Stomach – Structure and Functions

The stomach is a thick-walled, J-shaped muscular organ.
It stores food temporarily and mixes it with gastric juice.
Gastric glands secrete hydrochloric acid, pepsinogen, and mucus.
Hydrochloric acid kills germs and provides acidic medium.
Pepsin digests proteins into peptones.
Mucus protects the stomach lining from acid.
Improper protection can lead to peptic ulcers.
7. Small Intestine – Structure

The small intestine is the longest part of the alimentary canal.
It is divided into duodenum, jejunum, and ileum.
The inner lining has finger-like projections called villi.
Villi greatly increase surface area for absorption.
Each villus contains blood capillaries and lacteal.
This structure makes absorption highly efficient.
8. Role of Liver and Bile

rows: Completion of digestion and nutrient absorption
Absorption of water, minerals, and feces formation
Active digestion via bile, pancreatic, and intestinal juices
No digestion of food takes place

blocks.content:
The liver is the largest gland in the human body.
It produces bile which is stored in the gall bladder.
Bile does not contain enzymes.
It helps in emulsification of fats by breaking them into tiny droplets.
This increases the surface area for lipase action.
The liver also plays role in detoxification and storage of glycogen.
9. Pancreas and Pancreatic Juice

The pancreas is a mixed gland with endocrine and exocrine functions.
Its exocrine part secretes pancreatic juice.
Pancreatic juice contains enzymes: trypsin, amylase, and lipase.
Trypsin digests proteins.
Amylase digests carbohydrates.
Lipase digests fats.
Pancreatic juice acts in the duodenum.
10. Digestion in Small Intestine

Most digestion is completed in the small intestine.
Bile, pancreatic juice, and intestinal juice act together.
Carbohydrates are converted into glucose.
Proteins are converted into amino acids.
Fats are converted into fatty acids and glycerol.
These end products are ready for absorption.
11. Absorption of Digested Food

Absorption is the process by which digested food passes into blood and lymph.
Glucose and amino acids enter blood capillaries.
Fatty acids and glycerol enter lacteals.
Absorption mainly occurs in the ileum.
Villi and microvilli help in rapid absorption.
Absorbed nutrients are transported to different parts of the body.
12. Large Intestine – Functions

items: Bile is produced by the liver and stored in the gall bladder, but it contains zero digestive enzymes.
No digestion occurs in the esophagus or the large intestine.
Glucose and amino acids enter blood capillaries, while fatty acids and glycerol enter lacteals in villi.
Peristalsis is the involuntary rhythmic contraction pushing food through the alimentary canal.

blocks.content:
The large intestine absorbs water and mineral salts.
It houses bacteria that synthesize vitamin B and vitamin K.
Undigested food is converted into feces.
Feces are temporarily stored in rectum.
Egestion occurs through anus.
No digestion of food takes place here.
13. Digestive Disorders

Indigestion is discomfort caused by improper digestion.
Constipation is hard and infrequent bowel movement.
Diarrhea involves frequent watery stools.
Peptic ulcer occurs due to damage of stomach lining.
Jaundice is caused by improper functioning of liver.
These disorders affect nutrient absorption.
14. IMPORTANT FACTS – SSC FOCUS

• Digestion begins in mouth.
• Salivary amylase digests starch.
• Peristalsis moves food.
• HCl is present in stomach.
• Pepsin digests proteins.
• Liver is largest gland.
• Bile emulsifies fats.
• Small intestine is longest part.
• Villi increase absorption.
• No digestion in large intestine.
